text: Is GSE309890 the same thing as GDS309890?

## Abstract

This study addresses whether GEO accession GSE309890 is equivalent to GDS309890. Using a database query to the NCBI GEO accession resolver, both accessions were mapped to their respective records: GSE309890 as a Series (GSE) and GDS309890 as a curated DataSet (GDS), with separate entry types, unique FTP directories, and GEO URLs. The accession numbers are associated with different unique identifiers and types in GEO. This distinction matters for researchers selecting datasets for analysis, ensuring accurate citation and retrieval of the desired data.

## I. Introduction

**Background.**
The NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) uses accessions like GSE (Series), GDS (DataSet), GSM (Sample), and GPL (Platform) to organize expression data. Identifying whether two accessions refer to the same experimental data is essential for reproducibility and proper dataset citation.
  
**Literature Review.**
No literature was retrieved for this query.

**Knowledge Gap.**
Before database retrieval, it was unclear if GSE309890 and GDS309890 refer to the same record or different entities.

**Objective & Hypothesis.**
The objective was to determine if GSE309890 represents the same record as GDS309890. The hypothesis was that the distinct accession prefixes indicate different record types and possibly different content.

## II. Materials and Methods

**Study Design.**
A straightforward comparative analysis using the NCBI GEO accession resolver to map both accessions.

**Materials.**
- NCBI GEO accession resolver (functions.geo_resolve_accession).

**Procedures.**
- Input both accessions "GSE309890" and "GDS309890" to functions.geo_resolve_accession.
- Read out entry_type, unique identifier (UID), FTP directory URL, and GEO page for each accession.

**Statistical Analysis.**
No statistical analysis was required due to the categorical nature of the data; simple direct comparison of accession properties.

## III. Results

**Data Presentation.**

| Query        | UID       | Accession    | Entry Type | FTP Directory                                              | GEO URL                                                   |
|--------------|-----------|-------------|------------|------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| GSE309890    | 200309890 | GSE309890   | GSE (Series) | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/ | https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890 |
| GDS309890    | 309890    | GDS309890   | GDS (DataSet) | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/datasets/GDS309nnn/GDS309890/ | https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GDS309890   |

**Findings.**
GSE309890 and GDS309890 are not the same record; they have different entry types (Series vs DataSet), unique identifiers, directories, and GEO URLs.

## IV. Discussion

**Interpretation.**
The distinct entry types confirm that GSE309890 and GDS309890 represent different records in GEO. Although they may share content if GDS309890 is derived from GSE309890, they are not interchangeable.

**Context.**
These results relate directly to the database retrieval, which clarifies the organizational structure of GEO.

**Limitations.**
The record mapping does not establish whether GDS309890 was curated from GSE309890 without further metadata retrieval. It only traces accession equivalence, not content overlap.

**Conclusion & Future Directions.**
GSE309890 and GDS309890 are not identical in GEO. For full provenance or content relation, review supplementary files and metadata in each record.

## References

[1] GEO accession resolution results: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890  
[2] GEO accession resolution results: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GDS309890
